previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, alcoholic cirrhosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and prior right knee replacement presented with increasing right knee pain and systemic symptoms after completing a course of IV antibiotics for a prosthetic joint infection. She was found to have elevated inflammatory markers and was admitted for surgical intervention. She underwent removal of an infected antibiotic spacer, irrigation and debridement, and placement of a new antibiotic-loaded spacer. The postoperative course was stable, with resolution of fever and good wound healing. IV antibiotics were discontinued due to negative cultures, and she was transitioned to oral pain control. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with instructions for anticoagulation, wound care, and activity restrictions.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to internal joint prosthesis
Surgical operation with implant of artificial internal device causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication,without mention of misadventure at time of operation
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
